candidates.excerpt: The container shipping market is currently operating in an environment of unprecedented supply, with deployed capacity reaching historic highs across all major East‑West trade lanes. The charts show a monthly breakdown of the average weekly capacity deployed on Asia‑Europe. Instead of following the traditional late‑year taper following Golden Week, where supply typically contracts to meet softening Q4 demand, average weekly deployed capacity in October and November 2026 has accelerated dramatically, showing a complete detachment from historical trends observed in 2012‑2025. Deployed capacity on both Asia‑Europe trade lanes was elevated throughout the year, largely due to the Red Sea Crisis and the need for extra capacity to maintain weekly departure frequencies. candidates.excerpt: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators Kroll and StepStone Group have launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators to provide greater transparency into the use of non-cash interest in private credit markets. The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012. They measure PIK as a proportion of interest income, the percentage of loans with an active PIK component by deal count, and their share of outstanding principal. The indicators will also allow investors to compare PIK usage across geographies, sectors and borrower sizes. The launch comes as the firms’ data suggests PIK usage is moderating, with non-cash interest accounting for 2.86 per cent of interest income on loans originated globally over the previous 12 months, as of 10 October 2026. candidates.excerpt: CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering expects profit surge Container ship newbuild deals drive the company’s hitting 217% of its annual order target in nine months CSSC Offshore & Marine Engineering has forecast a notable jump in profits for the first nine months of 2026. The company projects its net profit attributable to owners of the parent for the January–September period to be between RMB1.10 billion and RMB 1.25 billion, a year-on-year increase of RMB 444.88 million to RMB 594.88 million, or a growth rate ranging from 67.91% to 90.80%. Its net profit attributable to parent owners is expected to hit RMB1 billion to RMB1.15 billion over the same timeframe, rising RMB 394.89 million to RMB 544.89 million from the 2025 comparable period, up 65.26% to 90.05% year on year. The strong expected performance stems from buoyant market conditions across the shipbuilding sector and solid operational execution by the firm.
